newsitem.title: FRANCE: Far right set to lose anti-EU French by-election.
newsitem.headline: Far right set to lose anti-EU French by-election.

text.p: A far-right candidate appeared headed for defeat by a communist on Sunday in a parliamentary by-election reflecting deep doubts in France about European Union integration.

Communist Roger Mei's office said partial returns gave him 57.5 percent of the vote to 42.5 percent for the National Front's Damien Bariller in the southern coal-mining town of Gardanne, where Mei is mayor.

Candidates for mainstream parties, from the conservatives of Prime Minister Alain Juppe to the opposition Socialists, were humiliated last week when they were knocked out in the first round and Mei and Bariller qualified for the run-off.

Both Mei and Bariller oppose plans for EU economic and monetary union including a single currency from 1999. Mainstream parties all favour the EU plan but are struggling to persuade an unenthusiastic electorate of its merits.
The by-election was for the National Assembly seat near the southern port of Marseille left open by the resignation of bankrupt businessman and former soccer boss Bernard Tapie.
